synopsis: EU Implementing Regulation 2022/1426 covers automated-driving-system type approval for fully automated road vehicles, not off-road machines; Chapter 10 nevertheless identifies its credibility framework as functionally relevant to off-road automatic braking [f7672, f2214, f8100]. The regulation is dated 5 August 2022, entered into force on 15 September 2022, and is cited in a consolidated version dated 24 March 2026 [f7671]. Annex III Part 4 requires documented model validation, manufacturer-defined acceptance thresholds, ODD-representative data, criticality assessment, characterized variability, and a defined envelope for using the virtual tool; evidence of team competence is also required [f7673, f7674, f7810, f10594, f10596]. Physical tests validate the toolchain and confirm the system, and Part 3 explicitly states that simulation shall not substitute for physical tests, qualifying Chapter 13's language about simulation replacing physical evidence [f7840, f10597, f10473]. Planning guidance recommends an early, two-page credibility-plan dry run against Annex III Part 4 to expose missing elements [f16536, f10922]. There is a cross-chapter scope tension: Chapter 3 says the regulation's contents were not reviewed, whereas later chapters provide detailed requirements and planning uses [f2214, f7674, f10922].
